**Issue #2516 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2516: Patch (part 15 of 19): compact the comments of the web's game layer
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

Part 15 of #2497 (compact whole-line comments, no logic change). **Paths, this part's alone:** every `.ts` and `.tsx` file under `apps/web/src/game/` (209 files, 0.50 MB of comments).

**Cautions:** `Game.tsx` is the one board, and each of its layers (animations, effects, audio, cards, drag, settings) has one owning module: keep the comments that say which. The client never enforces rules and never sees hidden information (CLAUDE.md rule 7), so keep comments that guard that.

**Web checks:** `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`; `pnpm --dir apps/web test`; `pnpm exec eslint apps/web`; `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Rules (from #2497)

**No logic changes**: nothing a test, a replay, a player or another service can observe may change. Edit only whole-line comments: a line whose first characters are `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*` or `/**`, and the lines inside a `/* … */`. Never edit a trailing comment, a JSX `{/* … */}` comment, or a line inside a string, raw string or template literal. Delete no file. Work through each file top to bottom.

- **Delete:** port history (the TypeScript version: `TS`, `ports.ts`, `packages/…`, `apps/server/…`, `PORT-MAP`, "as TS stored them"), keeping any rule or reason in it that still holds; change history ("used to", "previously", "formerly", "no longer", "renamed from", old version numbers; a card number like `C+ #29` is not history); a comment that only says what the next line plainly does; banner rules (`// ----…`, `// ====…`; a title between two rules stays, as one line); commented-out code.
- **Shorten** a block still over 4 lines to its why (the constraint, the invariant, the ordering trap, the ruling), said once; cut walk-throughs and examples a test already shows. Aim for 4 lines a block, 12 for a `//!` header; delete whole lines rather than reword.
- **Keep:** every cite at least once in its file (`R123`, `§9.4`, `CLAUDE.md rule 7`, `B36`, `#902`, "#442 L8"); directives (`eslint-disable`, `@ts-`, `/// <reference`, `prettier-ignore`, `SAFETY:`, `#[allow]` reasons, every `TODO` and `FIXME`), with no line added or removed between one and the line it governs; doc-comment fences (three backticks) byte for byte; cross-file contracts ("must equal …", "keep in step with …"); anything you cannot tell carries no reason. A smaller diff beats a wrong deletion.
- **Renames** (optional, minor): a function-local name of 25 characters or more (a Rust `let`, closure parameter or match binding; an unexported TypeScript `const`, `let` or parameter) may get a shorter one that is as clear. Only if `git grep -nw <name>` finds it in that function alone, the new name is not in that function already (a shadow compiles and changes behaviour), and the name is in no string, template, format string, object shorthand or destructuring. Never a `pub` or exported item, field, variant, prop, type, test name, or serde, ts-rs or Luau-kit name.
- **Target:** cut at least 30% of the part's comment bytes (#2497 needs 26% over all its parts), never at the cost of a reason. Measure before and after: `git ls-files <paths> | grep -E '\.(rs|ts|tsx)$' | xargs grep -hE '^\s*(//|/\*|\*)' | wc -c`.

**Check** from the repository root (`HEAD` is where this run started; #2497's reconcile runs the full checker against `origin/main`):

```sh
cargo fmt
git diff -U0 HEAD | grep -E '^[-+]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---) |^[-+][[:space:]]*(//|/\*|\*|$)'   # your renames only
C='\bR[0-9]+\b|§ ?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*|CLAUDE\.md rule [0-9]+|\bB[0-9]{1,3}\b|#[0-9]{2,5}\b'
for f in $(git diff --name-only HEAD); do git show "HEAD:$f" | grep -oE "$C" | sort -u > /tmp/c0; grep -oE "$C" "$f" | sort -u | comm -23 /tmp/c0 - | sed "s|^|CITE LOST $f: |"; done   # nothing
git status --porcelain   # only ` M` lines, all in this part's paths
```

If the first command prints a code line that is not your rename (often a call rustfmt joined once a comment inside it went), put the comment back. **Final message:** the byte counts before and after, every rename (file, old → new; the harness commits once, so renames cannot have a commit of their own), and what you left alone and why.

Its build lands on `bot/issue-2497`, not `main` (fullsend).

Part of #2497, split by Night bot (`opus`, [run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41066415581)).

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by Night bot (`opus`, [run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41066415581)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

1. Measure the comment bytes of this part's paths (Rules, Target).
2. Delete banner rules with a scratch script in `/tmp`: a line holding only `//`, `///` or `//!` and four or more `-` or `=` goes, and a title between two rules stays as one line. Run the Check.
3. Split the files into 6 to 8 batches by subfolder, one subagent each. Give each the Rules and this issue's cautions verbatim; each reads every comment in context and edits its files top to bottom.
4. Renames last, only where every rename rule holds.
5. The Check, then the web checks. Put back any edit that a check fails on.
6. Write the final message the Rules ask for.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->


<!-- jackioh-bot -->
````
